claim_one_line: CHARGE OR SYMMETRY AT FIVE (P-738, answered conditionally; the explore seat's test re-derived on main): in B355's level-5 Weil representation (projectively consistent on all 120 elements of SL(2,F5)), only +-I act as a scalar on both parity sectors (the charge premise = invisibility to every state), the projective commutant of rho(LR) is +-<LR> (the symmetry premise), rho(LR) is a Z/5 clock on every sector (eigenvalue angles 0, .4, .6 | +-.1 turns; traces 1 - phi and phi), the run of 6 has E = I (invisible to every state) while the line-invisible (2,1,1,1,2) has E = (LR)^1 (visible on superpositions of quasi-energy states) -- so the symmetry reading needs a superselection rule that would stop the level-5 clock, and under standard quantum mechanics and a physical level-5 Weil space the charge reading, and with it the run of 6, is the invisible one. 0 of 19. [CORRECTED 2026-11-10 (B1862; the advisor seat's audit, E3, reproduced on main): 'the charge premise = invisibility to every state' holds for E = +I only; rho(-I) is the parity operator, +1 on the even sector and -1 on the odd, so E = -I is invisible only on states of definite parity, i.e. under a parity superselection rule, a third condition; of B1853's 643 rung-invisible defects 338 have E = +I and 305 have E = -I; the run of 6 has E = +I and is unaffected.]
